name: Meridian Tactical Solutions Chemical Agent Poncho
description:
A lightweight, quick-deploy poncho that provides emergency protection against tear gas, pepper spray, and industrial chemical aerosols. The poncho seals at the wrists and neck with elastic gaskets and includes an integrated hood with a filtered face panel. It packs to the size of a fist and deploys in under five seconds.

Carried by protest medics, journalists covering civil unrest, and residents of districts where chemical crowd-control agents are deployed regularly enough to plan for. The poncho provides 30 minutes of protection — enough to escape the affected zone.
what_it_says: You expect to be gassed and you've packed a way to survive it.
story_hooks: A bulk purchase of 200 Chemical Agent Ponchos is traced to a civic organization that has never been associated with protests — someone is preparing for a chemical event that hasn't been announced.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, futuristic emergency cape that drapes from shoulder to mid-thigh when deployed. The silhouette is deliberately minimalist and unfitted — designed for rapid application over any clothing. When packed, it's an innocuous cylinder the size of a rolled fist on a belt loop or in a satchel.
physical_description.fit: Intentionally loose and one-size-fits-most; the poncho accommodates layered street wear, augmentation harnesses, or tactical gear underneath. The elastic gaskets at wrist and neck cinch tight for seal integrity regardless of body size.
physical_description.primary_material: Advanced ballistic-grade synthetic weave with activated charcoal micro-mesh laminate — lightweight but rigid enough to maintain shape during deployment.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, slightly tacky to the touch (adhesive gasket compound); the interior has a fine mesh texture visible through the transparent face panel. Some material bunching at compression seams from factory packing.
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte gunmetal gray with high-visibility phosphorescent yellow piping along hood edges and wrist cuffs. The integrated face panel is semi-translucent amber with faint targeting reticle etching.
physical_description.closures: Elastic gaskets with friction-fit grip at neck and both wrists; no traditional fasteners. Hood cinches via a single adjustable Velcro strap under the chin.
distinctive_features: Integrated molded hood with replaceable cartridge filter housing (two filter slots visible on right temple)
Semi-transparent amber face panel with micro-ventilation ports
Phosphorescent safety piping for low-light visibility
Compression pack attachment loops (often carries a pouch with spare filters and sealing salve)
Meridian Tactical Solutions corporate logo (chrome serif lettering) on left shoulder
Manufacturing date code and chemical resistance rating stamped inside hood seam
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 functional — affordable emergency equipment for working-class civilians and medical/journalistic professionals. Attainable for those who anticipate chemical exposure but not luxury goods.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by protest medics, independent journalists, environmental activists, and residents of industrial districts or heavy-handed enforcement zones. Signals preparedness, danger awareness, and implicit critique of civil authority. In the GLMZ, particularly common in South Chicago industrial corridors and Detroit manufacturing districts.
physical_description.condition_typical: Usually carried packed and compact, showing minimal wear until deployment. Active medics' ponchos show creasing, faint staining (chemical residue), and worn piping from repeated use. Filter cartridges are regularly replaced; older units may show discoloration in the face panel from aerosol exposure.
